The kitchen is small, so I couldn't tear down the sink or install a new one, so I requested a freestanding one and installed it. After installation, I put some old appliances on the countertop, such as a Nespresso Vertuo, blender, foamer, and electric kettle, and they are stable. First, since there is no dedicated detergent, I bought detergent today and tried it out. When I test-drove it after installation yesterday, the noise was so loud that it was annoying, but when I put the dishes in and turned it on, it was so quiet that I wondered if it was working. The noise and vibration were okay. I think the noise was caused by the water hitting the inside walls of the dishwasher in the empty space on the first day. If I was going to test it hard, I put in a pan where I coated pork belly, a cast-iron wok with mala-tang, and ceramics with lots of oil, silicone tongs, heat-resistant reusable containers, etc. and ran it on the standard course. The result was that the oil was completely removed from the coated pan, ceramics, plastic heat-resistant containers, silicone, etc.! The cast iron wasn't washed properly and still had some stains and food residue. The coffee cup didn't come off completely clean where the crema had touched. I think it's because of many variables, such as the amount of detergent, course, bowl position, and bowl shape. I'm a single-person household, but I'm a greedy maximalist, so I have a lot of dishes and a lot of trendy cast iron, so choosing the 12-person one seems like a great choice. Also, cast iron and large-sized cooking utensils are heavy, so my wrists were strained when washing them, but it's more convenient than I thought because I can just rinse them in a larva and put them in the dishwasher. The most satisfying thing is that I don't get my hands wet for a long time, I don't use detergent as much, and my stomach doesn't get wet! Although there aren't many dishes, they were oily, so I put in two water-soluble capsule detergents, and I didn't rinse them separately, but all the oil was removed and there were no remaining stains. You can choose the detergent you like~ When the washing is finished, the door opens automatically after the beep alarm~ The detergent inlet inside also opens automatically~ I should try drying later~ If only the delivery was not bad, I would have given it 4 stars. This made me think again about whether I should buy domestic brands, and when I asked the installers, they were not from the media, but rather outsourced the installation and some of the after-sales service to an external installation company, so it seems to be slow and unprofessional. As for the washing, the satisfaction level is about 80% at first glance. I wonder if the problem of the washing power or the material of the bowl itself is because the cast iron was not cleaned properly. However, as I mentioned earlier, it is convenient and I think it is cost-effective enough considering the price. The exterior is not pretty, but the cost-effectiveness makes up for it~ The operation is very simple and intuitive. It is also good that you can add dishwashing liquid in the middle~ The all-stainless steel interior seems hygienic. Freestanding tip? I've slightly modified the product review for Jeon Soo-cha. Since my kitchen is very narrow, I installed them as freestanding tables facing each other. I had to remove the table that was originally used as an island table, so I was worried about the space. Then, since the microwave and dishwasher are almost the same height, I bought a piece of 1200x600 pine board, placed it across, and covered it. It gave me a built-in effect and secured space. ^^ See the photos. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Sentence (English): I've slightly modified the product review for Jeon Soo-cha.
Comments (English): [ hmm.  ] || ---------------- || First, I was given the opportunity to use the product through the Coupang Experience Group. I chose the dishwasher, one of the so-called three aunts that are said to greatly improve the convenience index, and I was really looking forward to it, but the delivery made me lose interest and lose progress from the beginning-.-; After two or three days, I heard the reason, and it was even more absurd. They said that some of the materials were out of stock, so the delivery was stopped, and they told me about it and that they would install it around the 20th. I was completely shocked by the absurdity of the sudden statement-.-; I was trying to clean up the clutter of the table and appliances that had filled the living room to find the location and set it up again, and I was annoyed for the second time! Then, on the evening of the 14th, I got a happy call and they said they would come and install it between 12 and 1 PM on the 15th, so I told them to do so. As expected, they didn't come even though the time was up~ They called me saying they were late and came to install it after 2:30 -.-; The installation went smoothly after that, and they explained it well, but there was no specific reason or apology for the delay. The kitchen is small, so I couldn't tear down the sink or install a new one, so I requested a freestanding one and installed it. After installation, I put some old appliances on the countertop, such as a Nespresso Vertuo, blender, foamer, and electric kettle, and they are stable. First, since there is no dedicated detergent, I bought detergent today and tried it out. When I test-drove it after installation yesterday, the noise was so loud that it was annoying, but when I put the dishes in and turned it on, it was so quiet that I wondered if it was working. The noise and vibration were okay. I think the noise was caused by the water hitting the inside walls of the dishwasher in the empty space on the first day. If I was going to test it hard, I put in a pan where I coated pork belly, a cast-iron wok with mala-tang, and ceramics with lots of oil, silicone tongs, heat-resistant reusable containers, etc. and ran it on the standard course. The result was that the oil was completely removed from the coated pan, ceramics, plastic heat-resistant containers, silicone, etc.! The cast iron wasn't washed properly and still had some stains and food residue. The coffee cup didn't come off completely clean where the crema had touched. I think it's because of many variables, such as the amount of detergent, course, bowl position, and bowl shape. I'm a single-person household, but I'm a greedy maximalist, so I have a lot of dishes and a lot of trendy cast iron, so choosing the 12-person one seems like a great choice. Also, cast iron and large-sized cooking utensils are heavy, so my wrists were strained when washing them, but it's more convenient than I thought because I can just rinse them in a larva and put them in the dishwasher. The most satisfying thing is that I don't get my hands wet for a long time, I don't use detergent as much, and my stomach doesn't get wet! Although there aren't many dishes, they were oily, so I put in two water-soluble capsule detergents, and I didn't rinse them separately, but all the oil was removed and there were no remaining stains. You can choose the detergent you like~ When the washing is finished, the door opens automatically after the beep alarm~ The detergent inlet inside also opens automatically~ I should try drying later~ If only the delivery was not bad, I would have given it 4 stars. This made me think again about whether I should buy domestic brands, and when I asked the installers, they were not from the media, but rather outsourced the installation and some of the after-sales service to an external installation company, so it seems to be slow and unprofessional. As for the washing, the satisfaction level is about 80% at first glance. I wonder if the problem of the washing power or the material of the bowl itself is because the cast iron was not cleaned properly. However, as I mentioned earlier, it is convenient and I think it is cost-effective enough considering the price. The exterior is not pretty, but the cost-effectiveness makes up for it~ The operation is very simple and intuitive. It is also good that you can add dishwashing liquid in the middle~ The all-stainless steel interior seems hygienic. Freestanding tip? I've slightly modified the product review for Jeon Soo-cha. Since my kitchen is very narrow, I installed them as freestanding tables facing each other. I had to remove the table that was originally used as an island table, so I was worried about the space. Then, since the microwave and dishwasher are almost the same height, I bought a piece of 1200x600 pine board, placed it across, and covered it. It gave me a built-in effect and secured space. ^^ See the photos. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

전수차 상품평 수정을 약간함~ 주방이 ㄴ자로 좁아 마주보게 프리스텐딩으로 설치~ 원래 아일랜드 식탁처럼 쓰던 테이블을 빼야 했기게 공간 고민을 하다 마침 전자레인지대랑 식세기 높이가 거의 동일해 1200x600송판을 한장 구매해 가로지르고 덮었더니 나름 빌트인 효과와 공간확보가 됨^^ 사진참고~ 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

Comments (English): [ hmm.  ] || ---------------- || First, I was given the opportunity to use the product through the Coupang Experience Group. I chose the dishwasher, one of the so-called three aunts that are said to greatly improve the convenience index, and I was really looking forward to it, but the delivery made me lose interest and lose progress from the beginning-.-; After two or three days, I heard the reason, and it was even more absurd. I was completely shocked by the absurdity of the sudden statement-.-; I was trying to clean up the clutter of the table and appliances that had filled the living room to find the location and set it up again, and I was annoyed for the second time! Then, on the evening of the 14th, I got a happy call and they said they would come and install it between 12 and 1 PM on the 15th, so I told them to do so. As expected, they didn't come even though the time was up~ They called me saying they were late and came to install it after 2:30 -.-; The installation went smoothly after that, and they explained it well, but there was no specific reason or apology for the delay. The kitchen is small, so I couldn't tear down the sink or install a new one, so I requested a freestanding one and installed it. After installation, I put some old appliances on the countertop, such as a Nespresso Vertuo, blender, foamer, and electric kettle, and they are stable. First, since there is no dedicated detergent, I bought detergent today and tried it out. When I test-drove it after installation yesterday, the noise was so loud that it was annoying, but when I put the dishes in and turned it on, it was so quiet that I wondered if it was working. The noise and vibration were okay. I think the noise was caused by the water hitting the inside walls of the dishwasher in the empty space on the first day. If I was going to test it hard, I put in a pan where I coated pork belly, a cast-iron wok with mala-tang, and ceramics with lots of oil, silicone tongs, heat-resistant reusable containers, etc. and ran it on the standard course. The result was that the oil was completely removed from the coated pan, ceramics, plastic heat-resistant containers, silicone, etc.! The cast iron wasn't washed properly and still had some stains and food residue. The coffee cup didn't come off completely clean where the crema had touched. I think it's because of many variables, such as the amount of detergent, course, bowl position, and bowl shape. I'm a single-person household, but I'm a greedy maximalist, so I have a lot of dishes and a lot of trendy cast iron, so choosing the 12-person one seems like a great choice. Also, cast iron and large-sized cooking utensils are heavy, so my wrists were strained when washing them, but it's more convenient than I thought because I can just rinse them in a larva and put them in the dishwasher. The most satisfying thing is that I don't get my hands wet for a long time, I don't use detergent as much, and my stomach doesn't get wet! Although there aren't many dishes, they were oily, so I put in two water-soluble capsule detergents, and I didn't rinse them separately, but all the oil was removed and there were no remaining stains. You can choose the detergent you like~ When the washing is finished, the door opens automatically after the beep alarm~ The detergent inlet inside also opens automatically~ I should try drying later~ If only the delivery was not bad, I would have given it 4 stars. This made me think again about whether I should buy domestic brands, and when I asked the installers, they were not from the media, but rather outsourced the installation and some of the after-sales service to an external installation company, so it seems to be slow and unprofessional. As for the washing, the satisfaction level is about 80% at first glance. I wonder if the problem of the washing power or the material of the bowl itself is because the cast iron was not cleaned properly. However, as I mentioned earlier, it is convenient and I think it is cost-effective enough considering the price. The exterior is not pretty, but the cost-effectiveness makes up for it~ The operation is very simple and intuitive. It is also good that you can add dishwashing liquid in the middle~ The all-stainless steel interior seems hygienic. Freestanding tip? I've slightly modified the product review for Jeon Soo-cha. Since my kitchen is very narrow, I installed them as freestanding tables facing each other. I had to remove the table that was originally used as an island table, so I was worried about the space. Then, since the microwave and dishwasher are almost the same height, I bought a piece of 1200x600 pine board, placed it across, and covered it. It gave me a built-in effect and secured space. ^^ See the photos. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Sentence (English): Easy to install, works well.
Comments (English): [ Does the job, seems to be working well ! ] || ---------------- || Easy to install, works well. I just don't like that I need to press "Power" every time I want a cycle to initiate, or time it, or just start. I think just pressing Start should do whatever the last setting was, including the timeout to start., but, oh well. Has a dryer goop level detector. we use detergent with the drier already packaged but since I found a bottle under the sink, I decided to use on the new machine: it shut off the warning, but yeah, there is a setting where it will ignore that reservoir level.I had to run a new electric outlet because the previously installed washer had a simple wire that some lazy installer decided it would be great to just drill a hole through the floor. Like my granpa would say, "if you want something well done, do it yourself" - new outlet installed.LG decided to try to scrimp on the price by not supplying a power cord and the water inlet - yah, yah, every maker does that so, plan to spend another $30-40 bucks for the proper combo: water hose and power cord. The power cord is fine - anything you find on the appliances section for dishwashers will do. Water inlet is 3/8" MIP compression fitting, meaning you will need a 3/8" FIP compression fitting.The other side of the hose should obviously, match what it's under your sink. There is no need to use plumber's compound on these type of fittings. Watch out for the cord/water inlet combos as they have different connectors, so again, check under your sink.Water discharge goes into the garbage disposer (or a tap on the sink drain if your kitchen doesn't have a disposer). The machine comes with the metal clamp to secure the hose.Pre-installation steps, I found it waaaaay easier to just tilt the machine on its side to make the electrical and water connection - yup, remove the front black cover. Get some rags cuz there is leftover water inside from the factory tests. not much but enough to puddle.When pushing the machine in place make sure you have some space for the water discharge hose - it's kinda beefy and it may roll on itself behind the machine. needs some "let's try again" movement but, of course, eventually it gets in place. an extra 5-inches won't harm; or. the machine could do a better re-routing of that hose. Anyway, once it's in place, no more worries.I like it very much that it has a long screw on the front (behind the black cover) that allows you to raise or lower the rear feet to make the machine level: great feature since our kitchen and countertop is out of level alignment. I have no idea how that happened but it's been like that since we bought the house (yah, should have paid more attention, even for a first time buyer).Front panel is what I wanted: simple to use and has a nice white display that tells you how long (estimated) until the machine finishes the current job.I still could not determine if the front buttons are touch sensitive or chiclet type. most of the time feels they are touch sensitive but sometimes I feel I need to press more firmly or longer. we'll get used to it, I guess.Has plenty of space inside, and the bottom rack seems slightly lower than my previous machine, so that is a plus.Another nice feature is the "Overnight dry" where it (machine) will run the exhaust every so often during the night to release leftover steam and prevent bubbles streaks.It's not noisy either. I can't say much about the stainless steel but I like it. I can still stick our "dirty/clean" magnetic indicator - that thing should be standard on all machines :-)Overall I'm satisfied and would recommend it.

Sentence (English): First Secret: opening this dishwasher up - no manual.
Comments (English): [ This dishwasher has secrets! ] || ---------------- || First Secret: opening this dishwasher up - no manual. There is one. It's folded in half, hidden behind the glassware holder on the top rack, taped to the tub inside, left. You won't see it looking into the tub. Second secret: The hardware to complete the counter installation - is in a tiny package hidden inside the silverware holder. Yup, you find it by looking. If you find the manual, look for those brackets - it tells you to check the holder.Third: Hope you have a full set of 1/4" drive socket sets and tiny wrenches. Leveling - goes great until the 120vac power junction box gets in the way.Third: Quick guide spends a whole page on how to cut a 2.5" hole but never mentions where the power junction box is.Fourth: The drain hose. Comments (English): [ Super Quiet, get it! love all the new features ] || ---------------- || this is amazing! starting to begrudgingly having to replace older appliances. we bought this one because of the noise level rating, even though the handle doesn't match our other appliances. I use the tough setting all the time, i always have because my stuff can sit for a few days before i need to run it, although i don't put dishes in with tons of food on them, this cycle seems to work best for me. If you want a quiet dishwasher this is it! also the 2nd and third racks get cleaned really well as they have their own sprayer thing attached. oh and this one doesn't show prints at all! i love that because i hate stainless appliances for this reason. i barely notice and drips or marks it's stayed very clean and perfect looking!

Sentence (English): We bought a Bosch dishwasher, because they are reviewed as the best you can buy.
Comments (English): [ Bosch Ascenta Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We bought a Bosch dishwasher, because they are reviewed as the best you can buy. The best thing about it is that the dishes are incredibly clean after washing, which, of course, is important. However, there are a few things about the appliance that I'm not fond of. The first is that there is no drying cycle on it. In order for the dishwasher to completely dry your dishes, you have to buy a further product that will facilitate drying. We didn't want to have to buy an additional item which may or may not contain chemicals that might not be good for a person. The second thing I don't like is that the buttons for the dishwasher are on the inside rather than the outside. That has caused some problems with its use. The final item is that the way the dishwasher is set up inside, placing of various types of dishes, bowls, etc. is hard to do. It is not possible to get as many dishes inside, so we have to run it more often than we would like. I've read and re-read the user manual, but I've found that the descriptions of various functions are difficult to follow.

Folks complain they don't clean well and don't dry well. I found both of these complaints to be baseless with the Bosch. My Bosch dishwasher is very configurable and took some time getting used to. One feature can be improved I think. The bottom rack has space along the right for silverware containers which are not needed if you use the 3rd, upper rack. The right side is thus a good spot for large bowls or pots. However, also on the right side is a rack with an extra set of tines that, when popped up, can be used to support flat dishes. The same features is not available on the left set of racks. So, if you have a big bowl or pot, you can't use the right side for dishes. Note: if you put bowl on left side it intrudes too far to the right to use the racks on the right. It the popup tines could be moved to the left side I think things would work better.

Comments (English): [ Superior Machine at a Reasonable Price ] || ---------------- || When it became time to replace my 22-year-old dishwasher (also a Bosch), I put some time into researching the newest products, comparing features, prices. and availability. After all this preparation, I admit that I was disappointed once my SHPM78Z55N was installed and, after checking to ensure that it was working, the installer left The first time I tried to wash a load of dishes later than day, I couldn't get the machine to start. I went back and read the owner's manual again. Several other abortive attempts followed. The machine would come on, but within a couple of minutes at the most, the info light would go out and the machine would stop. Finally, luck smiled on me, though: the machine came on, stayed on, and when the wash cycle was through, the results were sparkling clean dishes. "Okay," I thought. "I've got it down now." You know what they say about pride and it's arrival. The next time I tried to start a load, I had the same problem. This time, luck didn't come to my aid, and the dishes were still unwashed the next day when my appliance dealer called to follow up on the installation and make sure I wasn't having any problems. I explained what was happening to him, and he suggested that I try throwing the dishwasher circuit breaker and letting it stay off for 10 minutes before trying to restart, so I did. I think luck was enjoying toying with me, because this time on the first try the machine started and stayed on. However, the next time I tried to wash a load, I was right back to the cycle cutting off almost immediately. An assessment of my predicament suggested the strong possibility that if the machine worked some times but not others, it was more likely due to operator error than machine failure, so I pulled the owner's manual out again and went through it page by page while standing in front of the machine. And, yep--operator error it was. I hadn't understood how to properly turn the machine on and off and had, instead, been punching in a setting that told the machine to do exactly what it had been doing. As the Germans would say, "Dummkopf! " So I'm now wiser and a happy camper. The Bosch does an outstanding job of cleaning my dishes. I love little things like the info light. The machine is so quiet that, especially after my rocky start with learning to operate it, it's nice to have that visual reassurance that there's actually something happening behind that closed door. I frequently find myself taking advantage of the MyWay Third Rack to gain space, and I really like the convenience of being able to not only raise or lower the top rack, but also to adjust the two sides independently of each other to make the most efficient use of space in all parts of the interior. Since I live alone, the ability to do a half-load is a nice feature. And Crystal Dry! When I'd read about it, it seemed too good to be true, but it actually works! No more plastic items that need to be put in the sink to finish drying after I empty the dishwasher. Given my age, the machine may well outlive me. If it does, it will add value to the house when the property is sold. In the meantime I'm enjoying my new dishwasher!

I tried tabs and liquid and long cycles but still had gritty film on glassware and dishes and pots. Also, the LG drank up rinse-aid like it was a person gulping water after a desert hike. The motor died right after my extended warranty expired. I had it replaced at my own expense. Then another year down the road, and it died again. Would never purchase an LG again. So on to Whirlpool. I use the dishwasher at least once a day, five days a week. That's a long time to go without ever having to refill the rinse aid. I have it 3 months now and it still cleans nicely no matter which cycle I pick. It does what it needs to do. It's not super quiet, but nothing that is disturbing while I am in the kitchen near it. I can easily speak/hear on a phone call. Overall, I am quite satisfied with the basic model that didn't cost a fortune.

I love cooking and eating, but I hate doing the dishes. My husband does most of the dishes, but I still wanted to make things a little more comfortable for us, so after much deliberation, I purchased a Samsung Electronics Bespoke dishwasher. I paid, canceled, and after much deliberation, I just bought Glam Pink! I didn't have to worry because the color is a more subtle pink than I expected. I think this is the best purchase I've made so far. If you're debating whether or not to buy a dishwasher, don't hesitate and buy it. Sentence (English): When it became time to replace my 22-year-old dishwasher (also a Bosch), I put some time into researching the newest products, comparing features, prices.
Comments (English): [ Superior Machine at a Reasonable Price ] || ---------------- || When it became time to replace my 22-year-old dishwasher (also a Bosch), I put some time into researching the newest products, comparing features, prices. and availability. After all this preparation, I admit that I was disappointed once my SHPM78Z55N was installed and, after checking to ensure that it was working, the installer left The first time I tried to wash a load of dishes later than day, I couldn't get the machine to start. I went back and read the owner's manual again. Several other abortive attempts followed. The machine would come on, but within a couple of minutes at the most, the info light would go out and the machine would stop. Finally, luck smiled on me, though: the machine came on, stayed on, and when the wash cycle was through, the results were sparkling clean dishes. "Okay," I thought. "I've got it down now.". You know what they say about pride and it's arrival. The next time I tried to start a load, I had the same problem. This time, luck didn't come to my aid, and the dishes were still unwashed the next day when my appliance dealer called to follow up on the installation and make sure I wasn't having any problems. I explained what was happening to him, and he suggested that I try throwing the dishwasher circuit breaker and letting it stay off for 10 minutes before trying to restart, so I did. I think luck was enjoying toying with me, because this time on the first try the machine started and stayed on. However, the next time I tried to wash a load, I was right back to the cycle cutting off almost immediately. An assessment of my predicament suggested the strong possibility that if the machine worked some times but not others, it was more likely due to operator error than machine failure, so I pulled the owner's manual out again and went through it page by page while standing in front of the machine. And, yep--operator error it was. I hadn't understood how to properly turn the machine on and off and had, instead, been punching in a setting that told the machine to do exactly what it had been doing. As the Germans would say, "Dummkopf! ". So I'm now wiser and a happy camper. The Bosch does an outstanding job of cleaning my dishes. I love little things like the info light. The machine is so quiet that, especially after my rocky start with learning to operate it, it's nice to have that visual reassurance that there's actually something happening behind that closed door. I frequently find myself taking advantage of the MyWay Third Rack to gain space, and I really like the convenience of being able to not only raise or lower the top rack, but also to adjust the two sides independently of each other to make the most efficient use of space in all parts of the interior. Since I live alone, the ability to do a half-load is a nice feature. And Crystal Dry! When I'd read about it, it seemed too good to be true, but it actually works! No more plastic items that need to be put in the sink to finish drying after I empty the dishwasher. Given my age, the machine may well outlive me. If it does, it will add value to the house when the property is sold. In the meantime I'm enjoying my new dishwasher!

It will eventually work. Sentence (English): My family purchased this KitchenAid Dishwasher (Model KDFE204KPS) on 08/22/2022, from the Lowe's in Montana to replace my 96-year-old grandmother's current dishwasher during a kitchen remodel to repair damage to her home.
Comments (English): [ Beware of Defective Units ] || ---------------- || My family purchased this KitchenAid Dishwasher (Model KDFE204KPS) on 08/22/2022, from the Lowe's in Montana to replace my 96-year-old grandmother's current dishwasher during a kitchen remodel to repair damage to her home. Like most kitchen renovations, the appliances arrived before we would need to install them, so it was stored in the house for a few months prior to installation when the remodel was ready. From the very first time it was installed, the dishwasher has not worked. After attempting basic trouble shooting for weeks, we were told that we must have a repairman come service the problem. The first visit was finally able to be scheduled for April 27th, and since that visit, he has returned a second time (and will be a third time). We have replaced the H20 valve, a leak sensor, and now have been waiting on the wire harness replacement (which apparently is backordered). We have contacted KitchenAid multiple times, and have been told we must continue to follow the repair path.Our manufacturer's warranty now expires in less than 30 days, and we will have a dishwasher that has not only never worked, but additionally has had so many parts repaired that our confidence level is zero that it will not need additional repairs in the future, which will now no longer be under warranty.This dishwasher is defective-has never worked, and has required multiple repairs, and is still unusable. That is not a “malfunction,” as mentioned above, this dishwasher is a “lemon” and KitchenAid should treat it as such. Instead we have a appliance that has been dead since arrival and a company that won't stand behind a clearly defective in more ways that one dishwasher.

Sentence (English): I wrote one review before.
Comments (English): [ Cleans better than my prior washer ] || ---------------- || I wrote one review before. I have had the dishwasher for a few weeks now. Here are some updates. No doubt, using the exact same detergent (Lemi Shine, Dishwashing Detergent Pods) that I was using before, the Bosch cleans better than my old LG washer (which was ~10 years old). I can really see the difference in a glass pan that I use to roast vegitables in olive oil in the oven. The Bosch successfully removes that burned on oil or the sugary residue from a roasted sweet potato in a way the LG didn't. I miss two things about the LG. The racks in the LG seemed to glide in a more sturdy way. The upper utencil rack in the LG neatly aligned my utencils in a way that Bosch grooves don't behave in the same way. That said, there is intention to the Bosch design. I find that I can easily fit a LOT into the washer at slight angles so that they drip dry. Finally, a key deciding factor in this model was the screen. In a household of a spouse and kids coming and going, the screen clearly communicates what is going on in the washer: is it running? dirty? clean?

Sentence (English): (This review was received through a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ Satisfied with the purchase ] || ---------------- || (This review was received through a promotion.) I've had the dishwasher for a short time, but so far what I've liked the most is that the dishes stay dry. The one I had before left it wet and I don't like that at all. I also really like the cutlery tray. They all come clean with no leftover food, as I sometimes did when I put them in the basket. The trays slide up and down easily and the plate holders can be folded down independently, giving you a little more flexibility. Although I find them somewhat bulky and when they are completely lying down, the dishes are not very stable. It is relatively silent. You can only hear the noise of the water caused by the sprinklers, but outside the kitchen you can no longer hear it. At the level of size it is a little deeper than usual perhaps. In my case, it protrudes a couple of centimeters from the kitchen cabinet. Configuring the application is a pain. When it works it's simple, the problem is that it doesn't work at first. Instead of searching the web, it is best to follow the instructions that come with the device, but if it does not work the first time (it will not work), start from scratch but wait more time at each step. It will eventually work. The truth is that I don't know if I will use it much, but now at first it has been more practical for me to configure the dishwasher (adjust the water hardness level for example) using the app than with the buttons on the dishwasher.
Comments (Original): [ Satisfecho con la compra ] || ---------------- || (Esta reseña se ha recibido a través de una promoción.) Tengo el lavavajillas hace poco tiempo, pero de momento lo que más me ha gustado es que la vajilla queda seca. El que tenía antes la dejaba húmeda y no me gusta nada eso.También me gusta mucho la bandeja para los cubiertos. Todos quedan limpios sin restos de comida, como me pasaba a veces cuando los colocaba en el cesto.Las bandejas se suben y bajan fácilmente y los soportes para los platos se pueden abatir de forma independiente, lo que te da algo más de flexibilidad. Aunque me resultan algo voluminosos y cuando están completamente tumbados la vajilla como que no queda muy estable.Es relativamente silencioso. Solo se escucha el ruido del agua provocado por los aspersores, pero fuera de la cocina ya no se escucha.A nivel de tamaño es un poco más profundo de lo habitual quizá. En mi caso se me sobresale un par de centímetros del mueble de la cocina.Configurar la aplicación es un rollo. Cuando funciona es sencillo, el problema es que de primeras no funciona. En lugar de buscar en la web lo mejor es seguir las instrucciones que vienen con el aparato pero caso no funcione a la primera (que no va funcionar) , empezad de cero pero esperad más tiempo en cada paso. Eventualmente funcionará. La verdad es que no sé si le daré mucho uso, pero ahora al principio me ha resultado más práctico configurar el lavavajillas (ajustar el nivel de dureza del agua por ejemplo) usando la app que con los botones del lavavajillas.

Comments (English): [ Satisfied with the purchase ] || ---------------- || (This review was received through a promotion.) I've had the dishwasher for a short time, but so far what I've liked the most is that the dishes stay dry. The one I had before left it wet and I don't like that at all. I also really like the cutlery tray. They all come clean with no leftover food, as I sometimes did when I put them in the basket. The trays slide up and down easily and the plate holders can be folded down independently, giving you a little more flexibility. Although I find them somewhat bulky and when they are completely lying down, the dishes are not very stable. It is relatively quiet. You can only hear the noise of the water caused by the sprinklers, but outside the kitchen you can no longer hear it. At the level of size it is a little deeper than usual perhaps. In my case, it protrudes a couple of centimeters from the kitchen cabinet. Configuring the application is a pain. When it works it's simple, the problem is that it doesn't work at first. Instead of searching the web, it is best to follow the instructions that come with the device, but if it does not work the first time (it will not work), start from scratch but wait more time at each step. It will eventually work. The truth is that I don't know if I will use it much, but now at first it has been more practical for me to configure the dishwasher (adjust the water hardness level for example) using the app than with the buttons on the dishwasher.

I've had the dishwasher for a short time, but so far what I've liked the most is that the dishes stay dry. The one I had before left it wet and I don't like that at all. I also really like the cutlery tray. They all come clean with no leftover food, as I sometimes did when I put them in the basket. The trays slide up and down easily and the plate holders can be folded down independently, giving you a little more flexibility. Although I find them somewhat bulky and when they are completely lying down, the dishes are not very stable. It is relatively quiet. You can only hear the noise of the water caused by the sprinklers, but outside the kitchen you can no longer hear it. At the level of size it is a little deeper than usual perhaps. In my case, it protrudes a couple of centimeters from the kitchen cabinet. Configuring the application is a pain. When it works it's simple, the problem is that it doesn't work at first. Instead of searching the web, it is best to follow the instructions that come with the device, but if it does not work the first time (it will not work), start from scratch but wait more time at each step. It will eventually work. The truth is that I don't know if I will use it much, but now at first it has been more practical for me to configure the dishwasher (adjust the water hardness level for example) using the app than with the buttons on the dishwasher.
Comments (Original): [ Satisfecho con la compra ] || ---------------- || (Esta reseña se ha recibido a través de una promoción.) Tengo el lavavajillas hace poco tiempo, pero de momento lo que más me ha gustado es que la vajilla queda seca. El que tenía antes la dejaba húmeda y no me gusta nada eso.También me gusta mucho la bandeja para los cubiertos. Todos quedan limpios sin restos de comida, como me pasaba a veces cuando los colocaba en el cesto.Las bandejas se suben y bajan fácilmente y los soportes para los platos se pueden abatir de forma independiente, lo que te da algo más de flexibilidad. Aunque me resultan algo voluminosos y cuando están completamente tumbados la vajilla como que no queda muy estable.Es relativamente silencioso. Solo se escucha el ruido del agua provocado por los aspersores, pero fuera de la cocina ya no se escucha.A nivel de tamaño es un poco más profundo de lo habitual quizá. En mi caso se me sobresale un par de centímetros del mueble de la cocina.Configurar la aplicación es un rollo. Cuando funciona es sencillo, el problema es que de primeras no funciona. En lugar de buscar en la web lo mejor es seguir las instrucciones que vienen con el aparato pero caso no funcione a la primera (que no va funcionar) , empezad de cero pero esperad más tiempo en cada paso. Eventualmente funcionará. La verdad es que no sé si le daré mucho uso, pero ahora al principio me ha resultado más práctico configurar el lavavajillas (ajustar el nivel de dureza del agua por ejemplo) usando la app que con los botones del lavavajillas.
